title: Types and symmetry: definable sets and automorphism orbits

based_on.title: An Introduction to Model Theory
based_on.pages: 27 (Lemmas 4.4.6–4.4.7 and Theorem 4.4.8), specialized to countable omega-saturated models and finite parameter sets; PDF dated 2021-07-13

based_on.title: Model Theory, Cambridge Part III, Lent 2023
based_on.pages: 27 (Proposition 7.5 and Theorem 7.6), orbit characterizations with explicit countable saturation hypotheses replacing the monster-model setting

summary: In countable saturated models, types are parameter-fixing automorphism orbits, and finite or singleton orbits characterize algebraic or definable closure.
abstract: If two tuples answer every formula with the same parameters in the same way, can a symmetry carry one to the other? In a countable omega-saturated model, it can when the parameter set is finite. This connects complete types with automorphism orbits. A point is uniquely definable exactly when all parameter-fixing symmetries fix it, and it is algebraic exactly when those symmetries give only finitely many images. The converse implications use saturation to turn a finite orbit into a single definition over the original parameters. For countably categorical models, finitely many definable tuple orbits give a further conclusion: a set is definable without parameters exactly when every automorphism preserves it.
